title: Prioritized temporal-stratified mini-packs for quant validators
creator: Sofia Lin
description:
Goal: produce compact, deterministic per-domain calibration 'mini-packs' sampled from live production prompts that balance recency, domain coverage, and rare-slot exposure so FP8/INT8 quantization profiles can be validated without running full traffic replays. These packs are intended for fast iteration (1k-20k examples) used by model onboarding, nightly accuracy validators, and CI gates for quant builds. The approach emphasizes deterministic sampling, repeatability across runs, and metadata-rich artifacts (domain, template_id, timestamp, slot_mask).

Why: existing large calibration bundles are costly to generate and run. We need smaller, high-signal packs that capture the distributional aspects most likely to reveal quantization regressions per domain (e.g., legal, search, chat, code completion). This ticket defines sampling strategy, pack spec, validation metrics, and rollout for automated checks in the quant pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling algorithm implemented as a reusable library callable from data pipelines and the CI job
Create deterministic per-domain mini-packs at sizes [1k, 5k, 20k] with metadata schema and S3 path naming convention
Run end-to-end validation comparing FP32 baseline vs INT8 and FP8 profiles on 3 representative domains; record token-level KL, task accuracy delta, and regression alerts
Establish automated CI gate rules: fail if absolute task-accuracy drop > 1.5% or token-KL > 0.08 on any domain-specific pack
Dashboards updated with per-domain calibration pack artifacts and comparison metrics
Documentation (Confluence) and a short tech-runbook for regenerating packs published
tasks: Design schema for mini-pack artifacts (jsonl) including fields: request_id, domain, template_id, prompt_text, context_slots, timestamp, client_hash, priority_weight
Implement deterministic hashing + reservoir sampling with temporal decay layer in sampling library
Integrate rarity-aware upweighting for low-frequency templates and named-slot preservation logic
Add CLI to generate packs from daily traffic export and store to s3://rwinference-calibration/minipacks/{domain}/{date}/{size}/{hash}.jsonl
Execute baseline runs: FP32, INT8 (symmetric + per-channel), FP8 profile A/B for three chosen domains (chat, search, code)
Compute and persist metrics: token_KL, perplexity_ratio, task_accuracy, hallucination_rate, latency_95pct
Wire results into Console observability: new tab 'Calibration mini-packs' with per-domain comparisons and historical trends
Write runbook and PRD snippet; add example usage to quant-pipeline CI (canary job)
Add automated regression alerts and rollback policy to quant build pipeline
notes: Sampling strategy high-level: stratify by domain -> within-domain apply temporal decay (recency weight) -> stratify by template_id -> upsample rare templates and long-tail slot combinations -> deterministic reservoir to meet target size.
Temporal decay: weight(t) = exp(-lambda * days_since_event). Default lambda tuned to ~0.06 (half-life ~11.5 days) for production conversational workloads; adjustable per-domain via config.
Rarity upweight formula: w_final = base_weight * (1 + alpha / sqrt(occurrences_template + epsilon)). Default alpha=2.0 to ensure at-least-1.5x sampling for very rare templates.

Slot preservation: when a prompt includes multiple important slots (user_mention, code_block, system_instruction), we preserve original relative ordering and do not truncate slot fields during pack construction. Pack consumers must support tokenizing with original slot markers.
Determinism: use SHA256(client_hash + date_bucket + domain + seed_salt) to assign selection keys; record seed_salt in artifact metadata to reproduce exact pack contents.
Pack sizes rationale: 1k for quick nightly sanity checks, 5k for CI gates on PRs affecting kernels, 20k for pre-release validation and quant profile final verification.
Artifact retention: keep last 90 days for per-domain mini-packs; snapshot accepted pre-release packs into archives for auditability.

Schema: a single-line JSON per example with flat fields only (no nested objects) to simplify downstream parsing by the quant-validator service. Example fields stored as strings to match existing artifact parsers.
comments: 2026-02-26 — Sofia Lin: Drafted initial design and shared with quant infra. Key decision: favor reproducible deterministic sampling over probabilistic streaming because reproducibility is critical for regression triage.
2026-03-01 — Arjun Patel: Implemented initial sampling library prototype. Verified determinism across runs with same seed_salt. PR: github.com/redwood/quant-sampling/pull/112

2026-03-03 — PM review (Evelyn Morris): asked that we include explicit customer-impact labeling per-domain and ensure legal/compliance domains get longer retention. Action: add 'customer_impact' tag to pack metadata and extend retention for 'legal' domain to 365 days.
2026-03-05 — Design (Marco Alvarez): requested example visualizations for Console tab; recommended a tile showing top 10 regressing templates per domain. Will follow up with mockups.

2026-03-09 — Arjun Patel: Completed integration tests for reservoir sampler + rarity-upweighting. Observed an edge-case where very high-frequency templates could crowd out medium-frequency ones; adjusted alpha floor and added per-domain cap on upsampling to 3x.

2026-03-12 — Sofia Lin: Launched first experimental run across chat/search/code domains using sizes [1k,5k,20k]. Collected metrics and uploaded artifacts to s3://rwinference-calibration/experiments/2026-03-12/ENG-340212/

2026-03-12 — PM (Evelyn Morris): noted early results show INT8 symmetric has small regressions in code domain on exact-token match tasks; recommended follow-up: increase exemplar density for code templates and add code-specific slot-preservation rule to avoid truncation of newline sequences.
